The repository itself carries no benchmark code or numbers; a paper-access retier could move it to B (peer-reviewed), but A is unlikely because the competitor framework versions, compiler flags and CPU model are not known to be stated.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Paper abstract (snippet only): 'in some cases more than 2x faster than other optimized frameworks for training end-to-end neural networks for speech recognition', and training times scale linearly to 64 GPUs (the highest tested) for models with 100 million parameters. The comparison against ESPnet, Kaldi and OpenSeq2Seq is in the paper's Figure 4 (training time per batch for a 30M-parameter recurrent model and a 100M-parameter convolutional model across GPU counts). The search record's 'more than 15% faster than the next-best system on a single GPU' figure could not be confirmed in any snippet seen in this verification and should be treated as unverified until the paper is read.
corrections.workload: Training time per batch (4 utterances per GPU) on the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) large-vocabulary task for a 30M-parameter recurrent acoustic model and a 100M-parameter purely convolutional acoustic model, scaled from one GPU up to 64 GPUs, against ESPnet, Kaldi and OpenSeq2Seq (paper Figure 4, snippet only).
corrections.caveats: Snippet only for the numbers: the README links the paper (arXiv 1812.07625, titled 'wav2letter++: The Fastest Open-source Speech Recognition System' on arXiv; ICASSP 2019 version) but neither the README nor the repository contains benchmark code or numbers, and arxiv.org, ar5iv, sigport, neurohive and similar mirrors were EGRESS_BLOCKED, so the paper's per-framework milliseconds-per-batch figure was never read. The paper is first-party (FAIR authors), measured in late 2018 on 8x NVIDIA Tesla V100 SXM2 16 GB machines against 2018 versions of ESPnet, Kaldi and OpenSeq2Seq; GPU training throughput there is largely set by the ArrayFire/cuDNN kernels underneath. The baselines are ASR training frameworks, not the video-audio category incumbents (FFmpeg, x264/x265, Opus); the project fits the ML-framework category better. The repository now redirects to flashlight/wav2letter and its README says wav2letter has been moved and consolidated into Flashlight (ASR application); reproducing its recipes requires Flashlight <= 0.3.2. Flashlight itself is already verified in wave 12 (autodiff-and-ml-kernels). Licence discrepancy: README says MIT, the LICENSE file is BSD 3-clause text (recorded as BSD-3-Clause). Recent commits (latest 2026-08-28, 'Fix B001: Replace bare except with except Exception') are automated or lint-formatting commits from the upstream monorepo sync, not feature development.
